rationale:
Final iteration. The race of this design is the last development race and the basis of the final unseen-track score, so robustness matters more than another experiment.

Evidence: Iteration 10 (search_right, otherwise identical to iteration 9) scored 703.76 against 704.85 for iteration 9 (last_direction). The oval and s-bend statistics are identical to iteration 9 to the last digit, so the loss response did not change those tracks. On the slalom, search_right lowered max_error from 0.0661 to 0.0646 and line_loss_events from 1.35 to 1.15, while the slalom still ended 0/20 off track. The score gap of about 1 point is within noise. Across iterations 3 to 10 the slalom max_error has stayed between 0.0618 and 0.0661 under every gain, speed, coverage and loss setting tried, so no tested lever has produced a slalom finish.

Decision: keep the iteration 10 design unchanged (base_speed 1.1, kp 2.6, ki 0.05, kd 0.9, sensor_weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], line_loss search_right, x +/-0.03 m at y 0.06, 16 mm footprint, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body 0.16 x 0.16). It is the design with the lowest slalom max_error and line-loss count measured, it matches the best oval and s-bend results, and the Evaluator approved it. I considered the search_left test the Evaluator suggested, but with no iterations left there is no later use for its result, and an untested loss direction could hurt an unseen track that resembles the s-bend or oval.

Expected result: oval and s-bend near 20/20 with completion times near 1.9 s and 2.25 s; slalom still off track at max_error about 0.064 to 0.066, unless the unseen track is easier. Hypotheses: (a) search_right gives a small slalom gain over last_direction; (b) speed 1.1 keeps s-bend completion_time under 2.5 s. Measurements requested: the full set, read per track, with emphasis on completion, completion_time, max_error and line_loss_events on any track that shows losses.
